name: PropertyBridge
headline: Property operations, connected.
summary: I led discovery, product definition, testing and launch—then followed through with onboarding, demonstrations and analytics.

sections.label: Product
sections.text: PropertyBridge helps landlords and property managers organise property records, tenants, rent, leases and operational work.

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: Manual tracking and disconnected records make it difficult to know what has been paid, what is outstanding and what needs attention.

sections.label: My role
sections.text: Product Management Lead at True Horizon Tech. I led research, product definition, pricing, requirements, delivery, testing, launch, onboarding and early analytics.

sections.label: My work
sections.text: I translated user and market findings into MVP scope and requirements, coordinated with engineering and stakeholders, and supported demonstrations and customer onboarding. I conducted internal alpha testing with colleagues and stakeholders, followed by beta testing with property managers, landlords, facility managers and lawyers.

sections.label: A delivery example
sections.text: Beta testers reported that some information failed to populate after Excel bulk upload. I worked with the developer to identify the affected fields and clarify expected behaviour. The issue was fixed and the information populated correctly afterward.

sections.label: Testing findings
sections.text: Feedback from both groups highlighted ease of use, smooth signup/onboarding and relevant functionality. These are qualitative findings, not an A/B experiment or measured onboarding improvement.

sections.label: Reported outcomes
sections.text: Over ₦500k in reported revenue. Revenue is an early commercial result, not annual recurring revenue. Separately, 11 demos were reported for July 20–October 7, 2026. Site-session growth of 138% and new-user growth of 230% compare August 1–31 with July 20–31, 2026. July is a partial month, so this is not an equal-duration comparison.

sections.label: Tools and environments
sections.text: Google Analytics; product documentation and collaboration workflows. Next.js, Clerk and Twilio are product technologies; their use is not a claim of independently implemented integrations.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: PRD, FRD, user stories, acceptance criteria, roadmap, competitor research, pricing definition, onboarding guidance and analytics requirements.

sections.label: Status
sections.text: Live product, launched 20 July 2026.

name: Chayim Diagnostics
headline: A clearer path to results.
summary: Customer feedback became a clearer results-access journey, alongside WordPress content and diagnostic test updates.

sections.label: Product
sections.text: A healthcare website with diagnostic test offerings and a patient portal for accessing results.

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: Users reported difficulty navigating from login to their results.

sections.label: My role
sections.text: I reviewed content and uploaded diagnostic test offerings using WordPress after the first build in 2023. In 2024, I reviewed user feedback, recommended improvements to management and supported interface/journey changes.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: The number of clients reporting difficulty accessing results fell from around 10 per week to 1 per week following the improvements. This is a user-reported operational measure, not a controlled experiment or a claim about all complaints.

sections.label: Tools
sections.text: WordPress; customer feedback.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: Updated test listings, reviewed content and recommendations for the results-access journey.

sections.label: Status
sections.text: Website improvements delivered.

name: LearnED
headline: Learning with fewer barriers.
summary: Personas, problem definition and market sizing for an inclusive, multilingual and offline-friendly learning concept.

sections.label: Product
sections.text: An EdTech concept developed by Team 4 during the Women Techsters Bootcamp with Tech4Dev. It proposes multilingual content, offline access and personalised learning for students aged 13–18, especially in underserved Nigerian communities.

sections.label: My role
sections.text: Group-project contributor

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: Language barriers, one-size-fits-all learning and limited inclusive resources can exclude learners.

sections.label: My contribution
sections.text: I developed user personas, defined the problem statement and contributed TAM, SAM and SOM market-sizing analysis. Other parts of the deck were collaborative team work.

sections.label: Tools
sections.text: Canva for personas; ChatGPT for research support; Google Docs for documentation.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: Persona designs, problem statement and market-sizing analysis, included in the team pitch deck.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: A group proposal connecting learner needs with a potential product direction. Market estimates are case-study assumptions, not measured demand. No user or commercial impact was measured because the product did not launch.

sections.label: Status
sections.text: Group case study · Not live.

sections.label: My role

name: RIO AI
headline: From intention to everyday routines.
summary: Research, strategy and requirements for an AI productivity companion for African young people.

sections.label: Product
sections.text: RIO AI is a web and mobile productivity and habit-building product for African young people. It is designed to help users build routines, track progress and stay accountable.

sections.label: Problem explored
sections.text: Difficulty maintaining focus and consistency, fragmented tools and limited visibility of progress. These are research and product-planning findings, not claims that competing products cannot address them.

sections.label: My role
sections.text: Product lead from ideation into development, coordinating designers, frontend and backend developers, Flutter developers and an AI automation engineer.

sections.label: My contribution
sections.text: Research, product strategy, roadmap, PRD and FRD; discussions on product design and architecture; team coordination.

sections.label: Planned MVP
sections.text: Daily/weekly goals and habits; commitment check-ins; task creation and reminders; daily streaks; end-of-day accomplishment reports; AI encouragement; basic productivity insights. The scope was documented using MoSCoW prioritisation.

sections.label: Tools
sections.text: Google Forms for surveys, Google Docs, Jira and Figma. Vercel and Render were used on the project, with infrastructure work handled collaboratively.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: Research, strategy, roadmap, PRD, FRD and reviewed product direction.

sections.label: Outcome and status
sections.text: Product definition completed and engineering work ongoing. All listed MVP features remain in development. The public landing page is separate from the unreleased app; no productivity improvement has been measured.

name: GroomingHer
headline: Growing with understanding.
summary: A Christian health-education concept for Nigerian girls, with connected girl, parent and school journeys.

sections.label: Product
sections.text: A clearly Christian health-education web-app concept for Nigerian girls, initially aged 13–15, with separate connected girl, parent and school spaces.

sections.label: Problem explored
sections.text: Girls need understandable education about body changes and a supportive way to ask for help; parents and schools need practical guidance. These are discovery assumptions to validate.

sections.label: My role
sections.text: Founder and Product Manager. I defined the first audience, education-first scope, user journeys, optional diary, chosen sharing, school pilot and implementation direction.

sections.label: Key decision
sections.text: The proposed first AI helper explains reviewed lessons; it does not diagnose, read diaries or automatically identify disease. This narrows an ambitious early idea to a more realistic first experience.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: PRD with user stories and acceptance criteria, README/product brief, design plan, implementation plan and proposed landing-page copy.

sections.label: Tools used
sections.text: OpenCode, Codex, Docker, ChatGPT Plus, Netlify and GitHub for AI-assisted planning and prototyping. Better Auth, Groq API and Resend are implementation choices, rather than completed integrations.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: A defined first-version scope and proposed six-week pilot. Healthcare review, school participation and funding are not yet secured in the current plan.

sections.label: Status
sections.text: Prototype in development. No live-user or clinical outcomes have been measured.

sections.label: What this demonstrates
sections.text: Product judgment, scoping, privacy-aware journeys and planning around real access constraints.
